fullPassage:
A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"

Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.

Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot that appears in most movies and TV shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset.

The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to fuel up for a hike.

While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.

Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture!

Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife. Watching people floating down the Merced River and hiking the Half Dome was cool. It was indeed a wonderful trip, with lots of laughter, joy, and sweat.

I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Let's get rolling! roll → rolling (get + -ing: ~하기 시작하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ roll → rolling: get + -ing(현재분사) = ~하기 시작하다. 'get rolling' = 출발하자
❌ ① feeling: 분사구문(동시동작). flew ~ feeling excited 정상
❌ ② assured: assure + 목적어 + that절 정상
❌ ③ landed: 과거시제 정상 (flew → landed)
det.tip: get + -ing: get going(출발하다), get rolling(굴러가다/시작하다). get + 동사원형은 불가

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 친절한 운전기사가 우리를 환영했고(welcomed), 우리는 출발했다. welcoming → welcomed (과거시제 동사)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ welcoming → welcomed: and 접속사로 연결된 두 절이므로 got과 병렬구조. 과거시제 동사 welcomed 필요
❌ ① which: 관계대명사 계속적 용법, cable cars 수식 정상
❌ ② riding: look forward to + 동명사(-ing) 정상
❌ ③ got: got on(탑승하다) 과거시제 정상
det.tip: 병렬구조: A got on ~, B welcomed ~, and C were off. 접속사 and로 연결된 동사는 시제 일치!

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 나는 비교해서 꽤 작다고(small) 느꼈다. smallness → small (felt + 형용사 보어)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ smallness → small: felt(느꼈다) + 형용사 보어. I felt small = 나는 작게 느꼈다. 명사 smallness(작음)는 보어로 부적절
❌ ① frequently: 부사, stopped를 수식 정상
❌ ② blowing: 현재분사, air를 수식(능동) 정상
❌ ③ which: 관계대명사 계속적 용법, Grizzly Giant 수식 정상
det.tip: 감각동사 feel + 형용사: feel happy/sad/small. 명사(-ness)가 아닌 형용사를 보어로!

det.korean: Dan은 Roy 삼촌이 나를 밀도록(push) 도왔다. pushing → push (help + O + 원형부정사)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ pushing → push: help + 목적어 + 원형부정사. helped Uncle Roy push가 정확
❌ ① smelled: must have + p.p.(과거 추측) 정상
❌ ② Thinking: 분사구문(이유). 빠르게 생각하며 → 능동 정상
❌ ③ yelling: 분사구문(동시동작). 던지면서 소리치며 정상
det.tip: help + O + (to) V원형: help him push/carry/move. -ing형은 불가. 사역동사 유사 패턴

det.analysis:
✅ ② extensive: 원문 'extensive public transportation system'. 광범위한 대중교통
❌ ① exclusive(배타적인): 대중교통은 배타적이지 않음
❌ ③ expensive(비싼): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ explosive(폭발적인): 교통과 무관
det.tip: extensive = 광범위한, 넓은. 비슷: widespread, comprehensive. 혼동: expensive(비싼)

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 극복해야 할 장애물과 맞서야 할 도전이 있었다. ignore(무시하다)는 부적절하며, 원문은 overcome(극복하다)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② ignore(무시하다) → overcome(극복하다): obstacles to overcome = 극복해야 할 장애물. 모험에서 장애물은 '무시'가 아닌 '극복' 대상
❌ ① fortunate(운이 좋은): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ courage(용기): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ next(다음의): 원문 그대로
det.tip: overcome obstacles = 장애물을 극복하다 ↔ ignore obstacles = 장애물을 무시하다. 모험의 교훈은 극복!

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"샌프란시스코의 역사적인 케이블카는 휠체어 사용자를 수용하지 못한다."

det.korean: 원문: the historic cable cars do not accommodate wheelchair users = 휠체어 사용자를 수용하지 못한다. 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문에 'do not accommodate wheelchair users'라고 명시
❌ F: 원문과 정확히 일치하므로 부적절
det.tip: accommodate = 수용하다, 편의를 제공하다. do not accommodate = 수용하지 못하다

questions.passage: The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests.

"요세미티 국립공원은 서울의 약 4배 크기이다."

det.korean: 원문: about five times bigger than Seoul = 서울의 약 5배. '4배'는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ F: five times(5배)인데 '4배'라고 했으므로 불일치
❌ T: five times ≠ 4배
det.tip: five times bigger = 5배 더 큰. 숫자 변조 주의! four ≠ five

"그리즐리 자이언트는 약 63.7미터 높이이며 거의 3,000년 된 나무이다."

det.analysis:
✅ T: 63.7미터, 거의 3,000년 → 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ F: 수치가 원문과 동일하므로 부적절
det.tip: about = 약, almost = 거의. 수치 문제는 정확한 숫자 대조 필수!

det.korean: 떠나는 것은 문제(problem)가 아니었다. 왜냐하면 이미 사진을 찍었기 때문이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ problem: 'That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture' — 사진을 이미 찍었으므로 떠나도 문제없다
❌ ① surprise(놀라움): 곰을 만난 것이 놀라움이 아닌 건 문맥상 부자연스러움
❌ ② success(성공): 떠나는 것이 성공이 아니었다? 논리 부적합
❌ ④ danger(위험): 떠나는 것이 위험이 아니었다? 문맥과 맞지 않음
det.tip: That wasn't a problem = 그건 문제가 되지 않았다. because절이 이유를 설명

det.korean: 내가 함께 가져가야 했던 전부는 용기(courage)뿐이었다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② money(돈): 여행의 교훈과 무관한 물질적 요소
❌ ③ equipment(장비): 휠체어 여행의 메시지와 부합하지 않음
❌ ④ patience(인내): 가능하지만 원문은 courage
det.tip: All I needed was courage = 필요한 건 용기뿐. 글 전체의 핵심 메시지: 도전 정신과 용기

ch: 피셔맨스 워프에서 점심을 고르는 데 30분이 걸렸다.
바다사자들은 가까이서 좋은 냄새가 나지 않았다.

det.korean: 바다사자들은 가까이서 좋은 냄새가 나지 않았다(didn't smell pleasant up close).
det.analysis:
✅ ② 좋은 냄새 안 남: 'didn't smell pleasant up close' 원문 일치
❌ ① 30분: 원문 'almost an hour'(거의 한 시간)
❌ ③ 방문 취소: 'delayed(지연)'이지 취소가 아님
❌ ④ 의류 상점: 'pretty shops and seafood restaurants'이지 의류 아님
det.tip: delayed ≠ cancelled. delay(지연) vs cancel(취소)는 다르다!

ch: Dan이 화자에게 핸드크랭크 자전거를 타보라고 설득했다.

화자는 핸드크랭크를 사용하는 데 끝까지 어려움을 겪었다.

det.korean: 원문: soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well(꽤 잘). '끝까지 어려움을 겪었다'는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 끝까지 어려움: 원문 'soon I was able to use it pretty well' = 곧 꽤 잘 사용할 수 있었다. 어려움 지속 아님
❌ ① 자전거 대여: bike rental service (일치)
❌ ② Dan 설득: Dan persuaded me (일치)
❌ ③ 터널 뷰 걸작: masterpiece painted by Mother Nature (일치)
det.tip: soon + able to = 곧 ~할 수 있었다. 적응에 성공했다는 의미!

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.

det.korean: 우리는 풍경이 점차 변하는 것(changing)을 보았다. change → changing (지각동사 saw + O + -ing)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ change → changing: saw + 목적어(scenery) + 현재분사(changing). 지각동사 + O + -ing = 진행 중인 동작 목격. 원문 'saw the scenery gradually changing'
❌ ① traveled → traveling: 과거시제 동사 traveled 정상
❌ ② bigger → biggest: 비교급 'five times bigger than' 정상
❌ ④ heading → headed: While heading(분사구문) 정상
det.tip: 지각동사(see/watch/hear) + O + -ing(진행) / V원형(완료). 여기서는 점차 변하는 과정 → -ing

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the __________ travelers in Northern California.

"Dan은 우리가 북부 캘리포니아에서 가장 __________ 여행자가 될 것이라고 나를 안심시켰다."

det.korean: Dan은 우리가 가장 멋진(coolest) 여행자가 될 것이라고 안심시켰다.
det.analysis: 원문 'we would be the coolest travelers'에서 coolest를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: coolest = cool의 최상급. the + 최상급: the coolest = 가장 멋진

questions.passage: Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to __________ us.

"곰은 우리가 싸온 냉육과 칩을 냄새 맡았음에 틀림없다. 왜냐하면 곰이 우리에게 __________하기 시작했기 때문이다."

det.korean: 곰이 우리에게 접근하기(approach) 시작했다.
det.analysis: 원문 'it began to approach us'에서 approach를 찾아 쓰는 문제. began to + 동사원형 구조.
det.tip: approach = 접근하다, 다가가다. began to approach = 접근하기 시작했다

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 글은 휠체어를 사용하는 화자가 친구 Dan과 함께 모험적인 여행을 시작하는 내용이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 휠체어 사용자의 모험: wheelchair + companions + challenges + 'Let's get rolling'
❌ ① 관광 명소: 아직 관광 시작 전이라 명소 소개가 아님
❌ ② 위험성: 겁이 났지만 긍정적 모험 시작 톤
❌ ④ 비행기 주의: 비행기 탑승은 배경일 뿐
det.tip: Let's get rolling = 출발하자! 모험의 시작을 알리는 문장. rolling = 휠체어 이중 의미

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 장애물이 있더라도 용기를 가지고 새로운 세계에 뛰어들어야 한다.
소셜 미디어에 사진을 올리는 것이 여행의 핵심이다.
혼자 여행하는 것이 동반자와 함께하는 것보다 낫다.

det.korean: 장애물과 도전이 있더라도 용기를 가지고 새로운 세계에 뛰어들라는 것이 요지이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 용기와 도전: 'All I needed was courage' + 'dove into a new world' + 'faced challenges'
❌ ① 완벽 계획: 계획보다 용기가 핵심 메시지
❌ ③ 소셜 미디어: 사진 정리는 결론부 소재일 뿐
❌ ④ 혼자 여행: Dan, Uncle Roy 동반. companions에 감사 표현
det.tip: All I needed was courage = 핵심 메시지. 장애물(obstacles)을 극복(overcome)하는 용기

questions.passage: Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a __________ painted by Mother Nature.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"요세미티 밸리의 터널 뷰는 자연이 그린 __________과 같았다."

det.korean: 터널 뷰는 자연이 그린 걸작(masterpiece)과 같았다.
det.analysis: 원문 'like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature'에서 masterpiece를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: masterpiece = 걸작, 명작. painted by Mother Nature = 자연이 그린 (수동태 수식)
